correctness.rationale: The neighborhood signatures on opposite shores lie in disjoint alphabets. Omitting two originals i,j while selecting k makes e_ik and e_jk collide; selecting no originals also fails. With at most one original omitted, subdivision signatures are distinct and nonempty. For originals, duplicate signatures occur exactly at two isolates or across an isolated chosen edge. A single isolate y is allowed only for OD and must itself be selected for closed domination. Removing y and its incident subdivision vertices therefore leaves exactly an OTD-code on the smaller clique subdivision, and conversely the lift introduces a unique empty signature without making any other signatures collide. There are n choices of y and the weight gains one power of z, giving nz P_OTD(H_{n-1};z) for n>=4, equivalently nz^(n-1)(z+n-1)W_{n-1}. Inclusion-exclusion over disjoint forced singleton and edge components gives W_s. For s>=3 the fewest edges form a forest of floor(s/3) components of size at least three, giving d_s=s-floor(s/3); Cayley's formula and partitioning the labels give B_s. In the non-total branch the minimum is n-1+d_{n-1}, attained by n(n-1)B_{n-1} codes. The total branch attains n-1+d_n in nB_n ways. Their comparison yields the gap and optimizer formulas. The frozen proof's generic edge minimum does not apply at s=2 (no eligible graph); the repair isolates n=3, where the non-total branch is absent, W_2=B_2=0, and there are nine size-four codes in both families. The original stated formulas were still correct in this case. No finite testing is used as a proof of the unbounded claim.
residual_risks: The lift relies on using all edges of a clique and distinguishing closed domination from nonempty open signatures. It need not extend to general subdivisions.

evidence: Chakraborty–Wagler prove gamma_OTD-1<=gamma_OD<=gamma_OTD for the relevant class; their clique example concerns the unsubdivided clique or disjoint unions of those cliques.

arXiv:2407.09692v2 gives general degree bounds and a subdivided-star analysis for identifying open codes, not this exact clique-incidence classification. A bounded term check in arXiv:2412.17469v1 did not establish any precise overlapping result.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general bound limits the gap to two possible values, but does not determine which holds in any congruence class of clique orders. Subdivided stars and cliques do not give the selected-edge partition mechanisms of the all-edge clique subdivision. Ordinary total domination on a central clique would not impose signature separation.

evidence: The foundational paper distinguishes OD from OTD, and equates OTD with open-neighborhood locating domination (OLD). The record 078f1db52295 calls precisely this latter notion an identifying open code, using the same graph S(K_n).

Under the conventional central-graph construction of a clique there are no original nonedge pairs to add, so that special case is also S(K_n); this alias does not identify central graphs of arbitrary graphs with full subdivisions.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Identifying open code, OTD and OLD all require nonempty distinct open signatures. OD permits one empty signature belonging to a selected vertex. This is an exact equivalence for the total subfamily and a real extra branch for OD, not a renaming.

value.rationale: The weaker code notion is genuinely different despite a general one-unit bound. The bijection identifies the entire extra population and expresses its distribution by an exact smaller-graph transfer. The resulting residue test determines when closed domination permits better optima, and the optimizer multiplicities explain the two coexisting mechanisms when the minima tie. This is a useful census of a natural infinite family, not a recomputation of the known OTD branch.
residual_risks: The result addresses labeled codes only, not automorphism classes, and adopts the stated OD/OTD definitions rather than other notions of identifying code.
